import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 as instructed
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_8.csv", index_col=0)
source9 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/training_9.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source4 (boro, zipcode) with Source0 (crime data) on zipcode
df = source4.merge(source0, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Join Source4 with Source5 (theft, assault, harassment) on zipcode
df = df.merge(source5, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Join Source4 with Source2 (indicator, counts) on zipcode
df = df.merge(source2, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Union business tables: Source1, Source3, Source7, Source9
businesses = pd.concat([source1, source3, source7, source9], ignore_index=True)

# Group by zipcode and businesses to sum counts in unioned business data
businesses_agg = businesses.groupby(["zipcode", "businesses"], as_index=False).agg({"counts": "sum"})

# Join unioned business data with Source4 on zipcode and businesses
df = df.merge(businesses_agg, on=["zipcode"], how="inner", suffixes=("", "_business"))
df = df.merge(businesses_agg, left_on=["zipcode", "businesses"], right_on=["zipcode", "businesses"], how="inner", suffixes=("", "_business"))

# Join Source6 (zipcode, counts) on zipcode
df = df.merge(source6, on="zipcode", how="inner", suffixes=("", "_6"))

# Join Source8 (zipcode, counts) on zipcode
df = df.merge(source8, on="zipcode", how="inner", suffixes=("", "_8"))

# Group by zipcode, boro, indicator to aggregate counts and crime data
final = df.groupby(["zipcode", "boro", "indicator"], as_index=False).agg({
    "counts": "sum",
    "total_crime": "sum",
    "violation": "sum",
    "misdemeanor": "sum",
    "felony": "sum",
    "theft": "sum",
    "assault": "sum",
    "harassment": "sum",
    "counts_6": "sum",
    "counts_8": "sum"
})

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# The target schema has multiple businesses and counts columns with suffixes _x, _y, _x_5, _x_6, _y_7, _y_8, counts_x_10, counts_y_11
# We need to reconstruct these columns carefully from the unioned business data and joins.

# To reconstruct the multiple business/counts columns, we do the following:

# We have four business types from unioned tables: Pawnbroker (source1), Debt Collection Agency (source3), Cigarette Retail Dealer (source7), Sidewalk Cafe (source9)
# We want to pivot the unioned business counts to separate columns for each business type

# Pivot unioned business counts
business_pivot = businesses.pivot_table(index="zipcode", columns="businesses", values="counts", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema:
# From target examples:
# businesses_x: Pawnbroker
# counts_x: Pawnbroker counts
# businesses_y: Sidewalk Cafe
# counts_y: Sidewalk Cafe counts
# businesses_x_5: Debt Collection Agency
# counts_x_6: Debt Collection Agency counts
# businesses_y_7: Cigarette Retail Dealer
# counts_y_8: Cigarette Retail Dealer counts

# Create a DataFrame with these columns
business_cols = {
    "businesses_x": "Pawnbroker",
    "counts_x": "Pawnbroker",
    "businesses_y": "Sidewalk Cafe",
    "counts_y": "Sidewalk Cafe",
    "businesses_x_5": "Debt Collection Agency",
    "counts_x_6": "Debt Collection Agency",
    "businesses_y_7": "Cigarette Retail Dealer",
    "counts_y_8": "Cigarette Retail Dealer"
}

# Create a DataFrame with zipcode and these columns
business_df = pd.DataFrame()
business_df["zipcode"] = business_pivot["zipcode"]

for col_name, business_name in business_cols.items():
    if "businesses" in col_name:
        # business name columns: fill with constant business name if zipcode exists in pivot, else NaN
        business_df[col_name] = business_name
    else:
        # counts columns: get counts from pivot, fill 0 if missing
        business_df[col_name] = business_pivot.get(business_name, pd.Series(dtype=int)).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Merge business_df with df on zipcode
df = df.merge(business_df, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Now df has all columns, but some counts columns from source6 and source8 need to be renamed to counts_x_10 and counts_y_11
df = df.rename(columns={
    "counts": "counts_x_10",  # from source6 counts (joined last)
    "counts_6": "counts_y_11"  # from source8 counts
})

# The indicator and counts columns from source2 are already in df as 'indicator' and 'counts' (from source2)
# But we renamed counts from source2 to counts_x_10 above, so we need to fix that:

# Actually, source2 counts is 'counts' column before renaming, but we renamed counts from source6 to counts_x_10 and counts from source8 to counts_y_11
# So we need to keep source2 counts as 'counts' column

# To avoid confusion, let's re-merge source2 indicator and counts separately:

df = df.drop(columns=["indicator", "counts"], errors='ignore')
df = df.merge(source2, on="zipcode", how="inner")

# Final columns order as per target schema:
final_columns = [
    "zipcode",
    "businesses_x",
    "counts_x",
    "businesses_y",
    "counts_y",
    "businesses_x_5",
    "counts_x_6",
    "businesses_y_7",
    "counts_y_8",
    "boro",
    "counts_x_10",
    "counts_y_11",
    "indicator",
    "counts",
    "total_crime",
    "violation",
    "misdemeanor",
    "felony",
    "theft",
    "assault",
    "harassment"
]

# Select and reorder columns
final = df[final_columns]

# Save to CSV
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_18/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
